title: Pretraining
description: Training a model from scratch on raw text using next-token prediction.
whenToUse: You want to create a new foundation model or train on a completely new language/domain.
whyNotOthers: Most expensive and data-hungry. Only choose when fine-tuning cannot achieve your goal.
dataRequired: Billions to trillions of tokens. Cleaned, deduplicated, filtered text.
hardware: Multi-GPU (8+ H100/A100) for models >1B. Single GPU for <100M parameter models.
typicalLR: 3e-4 peak (7B scale), 1-3% warmup, cosine decay to 10%
steps: Fix token budget (Chinchilla ~20 tok/param minimum)
Set tokens/step from hardware (batch x seq x GPUs)
LR warmup then cosine decay over the full horizon
Train with BF16 + AdamW + grad clip 1.0
Checkpoint regularly; watch loss curve + MFU
Evaluate on downstream suites, not just perplexity
expectedResult: Smoothly falling loss following a power-law trend; downstream capability grows with tokens.
failureModes: Loss spikes (LR/batch too aggressive); silent divergence (loss falls, evals flat - data mix issue); NaN (precision/warmup).
vramNote: Full Adam training ~16 bytes/param + activations. 7B needs ~8x80GB class hardware. Verify with the VRAM calculator.

title: Continued Pretraining
description: Continuing to train an existing model on new data to expand its knowledge or adapt to a new domain.
whenToUse: You have domain-specific text and want the model to learn new facts/patterns without changing its basic behavior.
whyNotOthers: Better than fine-tuning when the new data is large (millions of tokens) and similar in format to pretraining data.
dataRequired: Millions to billions of tokens of domain text.
hardware: Similar to pretraining but can start with fewer GPUs if model is frozen except last layers.
steps: Curate domain corpus (millions+ tokens, quality-filtered)
Mix 5-20% general replay data
Train at low LR with short warmup
Monitor domain PPL + general benchmarks jointly
SFT after CPT for instruction behavior
expectedResult: Domain perplexity falls with general scores roughly preserved (small measured trade acceptable).
failureModes: Catastrophic forgetting (LR too high, no replay); SFT-format damage (CPT raw text degrades instruction manners - re-SFT after).
vramNote: Same as pretraining for the model size. LoRA-CPT hybrids exist but lag full CPT on heavy domain shifts.

title: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT)
description: Training a model on input-output pairs to teach it to follow instructions.
whenToUse: You want the model to respond in a specific format or follow instructions for a specific task.
whyNotOthers: Use SFT when you have labeled examples. Use continued pretraining when you have raw domain text.
dataRequired: Thousands to hundreds of thousands of instruction-response pairs.
hardware: Single GPU (with LoRA) to multi-GPU (full fine-tuning).
steps: Format data with the model's chat template
Mask prompt tokens from the loss (train on responses)
Train 1-3 epochs with warmup
Evaluate on held-out instructions + general benchmarks
Check for forgetting before shipping
expectedResult: Instruction following improves; general capability roughly preserved (within ~1-2%).
failureModes: Forgetting (too much LR/epochs); format leakage (everything answered in template style); verbosity bias from long chosen responses.
vramNote: Full SFT same cost as pretraining per token; LoRA-SFT a fraction (see LoRA).

title: LoRA
description: Low-Rank Adaptation: freeze the base model and train small rank-decomposition matrices attached to selected layers.
whenToUse: GPU memory is limited but you want better results than prompt engineering. The standard approach for fine-tuning.
whyNotOthers: Slightly less capable than full fine-tuning, but uses ~10x less memory. Choose full FT only if you have the hardware.
dataRequired: Similar to SFT: thousands to hundreds of thousands of examples.
hardware: Single consumer GPU (24GB) for 7B models. Multi-GPU for larger models.
steps: Choose rank (16-32 start) and target all linear layers
Format data as for SFT (template + masking)
Train adapters, base frozen
Evaluate vs base and vs full-FT probe
Merge for single-task serving, or serve unmerged multi-adapter
expectedResult: Near full-FT quality on near-domain tasks at ~1% trainable params.
failureModes: Underfitting at low rank on knowledge-heavy shifts (raise rank or CPT first); merged dtype mismatch; evaluating with adapter detached.
vramNote: Gradients + Adam states on adapters only. 7B LoRA fits 24GB; see VRAM calculator with LoRA enabled.

title: QLoRA
description: LoRA combined with 4-bit quantization of the base model. Enables fine-tuning 7B models on a single 8GB GPU.
whenToUse: You have very limited GPU memory (8-12GB) but want to fine-tune a large model.
whyNotOthers: Slightly lower quality than full LoRA due to quantization noise. But often good enough, and dramatically cheaper.
steps: Load base in NF4 4-bit (keep compute BF16)
Attach LoRA adapters (r=32, alpha=64 typical)
Train with gradient accumulation to effective batch 32+
Evaluate quality gap vs full LoRA on your evals
Serve unmerged or dequantize-merge-requantize
expectedResult: ~99% of SFT quality on instruction tasks at <10GB for 7B.
failureModes: Quality gap concentrates on math/code/rare languages (verify, don't assume); OOM from batch (accumulate more); quantizing adapters too.
vramNote: Frozen base ~0.55 bytes/param effective (NF4 + group scales, not raw 0.5). Full-precision training on adapters only. 7B QLoRA fits 8-12GB GPUs.

title: DPO (Direct Preference Optimization)
description: Align model behavior using preference pairs instead of training a separate reward model.
whenToUse: You have preference data (chosen/rejected responses) and want to align the model without RL.
whyNotOthers: Simpler than RLHF (no reward model, no PPO). But requires preference data which is harder to collect than instruction data.
dataRequired: Preference pairs: (chosen_response, rejected_response) for many prompts.
typicalLR: 5e-7 to 5e-6 typical (lower than SFT), beta 0.05-0.5, 1 epoch
steps: Collect chosen/rejected pairs differing in target behavior
Start from the SFT model (+ frozen reference copy)
Train ~1 epoch watching the chosen-rejected margin
Evaluate alignment + capability retention
Length-normalize or balance pair lengths
expectedResult: Preference alignment improves without capability loss; margin rises while both likelihoods stay healthy.
failureModes: Likelihood collapse (both fall - raise beta, shorten run); verbosity hacking (chosen longer on average); noisy pairs teaching noise.
vramNote: Needs policy + reference model in memory (~2x SFT inference footprint during training).

title: RLHF
description: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback. Train a reward model, then optimize the LLM with PPO.
whenToUse: You need the most sophisticated alignment. The original InstructGPT/ChatGPT approach.
whyNotOthers: Much more complex than DPO. Three models needed (LLM, reward, reference) instead of DPO's two. DPO is usually sufficient.
dataRequired: ranked responses for reward model training + preference data for RL.
hardware: More GPUs than DPO (need room for reward model + reference model).
steps: SFT baseline first
Train reward model (validate pairwise accuracy 65%+)
PPO with KL anchor to the SFT model
Monitor proxy reward AND held-out human judgment
Stop on reward over-optimization, not max reward
expectedResult: Best alignment quality when done well; requires the full pipeline firing.
failureModes: Reward hacking (proxy up, humans down); PPO collapse (clip/KL mis-tuning); forgetting (KL too loose). Try DPO first.
vramNote: Policy + reference + reward + value models live during PPO - the most memory-hungry alignment method.
